identity.name: Roland Steinhauer
identity.role: co-founder and chief technology officer, Hudson Valley Biometrics (adverse party representative)

background: Co-founder and CTO of Hudson Valley Biometrics and the executive who drove the decision to send the cease-and-desist letter and to move for a preliminary injunction against Priya Iyer. He is the company's declarant on the motion. As a management-level representative of the plaintiff company, he is represented by Hudson Valley Biometrics's counsel for purposes of this dispute.
personality: Confident, founder-proud, and protective of the company he built. He believes the matching engine is Hudson Valley's whole value and takes the loss of its technical lead to a competitor as both a security threat and a personal betrayal.
emotional_state: Composed but aggrieved; he frames the case as protecting years of investment and treats Iyer's departure as a breach of trust.
communication_style: Speaks in polished founder-and-investor terms and sticks to the company line about the engine being proprietary; grows noticeably vaguer when pressed on how openly the code was actually shared or on what specific thing he says was taken.

objectives: Enforce the non-compete and keep Iyer out of a competitor
Protect what he calls the company's crown-jewel matching engine
Deter other engineers from leaving for rivals
fears: That the engine will be shown to rest on public research and loose internal handling
That the real reason — losing a big bid to Sightline — will surface
Losing more of his engineering team

rule_4_2.counsel_name: Halbrook Renner & Iselin LLP (counsel for Hudson Valley Biometrics, Inc.)
rule_4_2.teaching_moment: Roland Steinhauer is a co-founder and management-level representative of the represented adverse party, Hudson Valley Biometrics. Under the no-contact rule, defense counsel may not communicate with him about the subject of the representation without the consent of Hudson Valley's counsel. Seek information through his counsel or through formal discovery — a deposition, an interrogatory, a document request — rather than contacting him directly.

volunteered.text: That matching engine is the crown jewel of this company. We spent years and a fortune building it, and Ms. Iyer knew every corner of it before she walked out the door to a competitor.

revealed_if_asked.text: The agreement is two years, and yes, it covers biometric and computer-vision matching generally. Every engineer signs it — it's a condition of employment, and it exists precisely to protect what she knows.

It doesn't matter whether she copied a file. She knows our engine cold. There is no way she can build a competing vision product without inevitably using what she learned here. That's the whole point.

rapport_gated.text: Well — the code did live in shared repositories, and the team did talk about the architecture openly in engineering meetings. That's how a fast startup works. It wasn't compartmentalized the way a big defense contractor might do it.

No, there wasn't one document stamped 'trade secret' that describes the whole engine. People just understood the system was sensitive. If you're asking me to point to the single secret she took, it's the accumulated know-how, not a file.

concealed.text: The timing isn't an accident. We lost a county-wide public-safety bid to Sightline two months before she quit, and I am not going to pretend that drawing this line — for her and for everyone else watching — isn't part of what this is about.

unknown.text: Do I have proof she actually took something? Not a specific file, no. I'm telling you what I'm sure of from how much she knew. I haven't seen a smoking gun and I'm not going to invent one.

knowledge_boundary.unknown_response_style: I couldn't tell you specifically / that's outside what I handle personally.
color_topics: his collection of vintage analog synthesizers
weekend sailing on the Hudson and the marina near Kingston
